title: Person recognition: CLIP-ViT-B/32 body embedding + VM2 feature matching for enrolled person re-identification
author: jill (operator-directed 2026-09-26, V2-059 PRD draft)
plan_section: v2 person identity recognition: embed enrolled person images into 512-dim CLIP-ViT-B/32 vectors, run Tier-2 embedding cosine on every person alert, Tier-1 VM2 feature scoring for advisory ranking among cosine-acceptable candidates -- paralleling how animal recognition uses MegaDescriptor-L-384
trigger: Operator 2026-09-26: person recognition is the parallel capability to animal recognition (V2-045). Animal branch (Finnegan enrolled, Finnegan recognized) demonstrated the embedding-based re-ID pipeline. Same pattern for people: enroll operator-known persons, then recognize them on alerts. V2-032 PRD covered a text-only tag+Jaccard matcher (person_matcher/match.py already exists, wired into pipeline stage 12). That matcher is sufficient as Tier-1 advisory, but the PRD needs Tier-2 embedding cosine as the PRIMARY match signal (operator directive, same as animal: Tier 2 always runs). Infrastructure already exists: infra/person_embedder.py (CLIP-ViT-B/32, 512-dim), scripts/enroll_person.py (CLI), data/known/people/ (storage), person_matcher/match.py (tag+Jaccard). The gap: person_embedder.py uses CLIP-ViT-B/32 (not OSNet -- torchreid unavailable on Apple Silicon), Tier-2 cosine matching is not wired into the alert pipeline, and the enrollment CLI does not produce embeddings.npz for Tier-2 (it exists but needs Tier-2 threshold config). Three concrete gaps: (1) Pipeline Stage 12 calls match_person() (text-only tag+Jaccard) but does not run CLIP embedding cosine as a primary signal. (2) No Tier-2 cosine threshold config for person matching. (3) No person-aware TG#3 caption that shows embedding-based match confidence.
background: v2 currently has person matching via person_matcher.match_person() -- a pure text-based matcher that does tag exact-match (case-insensitive, whitespace-stripped) then Jaccard >= 0.5 on identity_markers. This is sufficient for simple cases (e.g. operator recognizes 'red-jacket-beard' as a known person) but has no embedding-based re-ID. Animal recognition (V2-045) demonstrated that Tier-2 embedding cosine (MegaDescriptor-S-224, 768-dim) provides reliable individual recognition across different crops/lighting. Person recognition needs the same: Tier-2 CLIP body-shape embedding cosine (always runs on every person alert) + Tier-1 tag+Jaccard (advisory ranking). Model: CLIP-ViT-B/32 from openai (hf-hub:openai/clip-vit-base-patch32), 512-dim embeddings, already implemented in infra/person_embedder.py. Weights: ~250MB, downloaded via timm into ~/Library/Caches/huggingface/hub/. Empirical rationale: CLIP-ViT-B/32 was trained on LAION-2B (400M image-text pairs), produces body-shape embeddings suitable for re-ID at small scale. While not OSNet (torchreid unavailable on Apple Silicon), it serves the same purpose. Already wired into pipeline: person_matcher.match_person() at listener/pipeline.py:251, _load_person_candidates() at listener/pipeline.py:88, TG#3 build at stage_build_tg3 (line 260) dispatches person mode to build_match_message().

design_principles: Tier 2 (CLIP-ViT-B/32 cosine) ALWAYS runs on every person alert (operator directive, same as animal: Tier 2 is the PRIMARY match signal). Tier 2 is the primary accept gate -- if no enrolled person has cosine >= TIER2_THRESHOLD (default 0.80), the alert is 'unrecognized person'. Tier 1 (tag+Jaccard) is ADVISORY -- it ranks the cosine-acceptable candidates and provides metadata for TG#3 rendering.

Match flow: (1) Stage 11b picks the chosen crop via better_crop. (2) CLIP-ViT-B/32 embeds it -> observed_embedding. (3) Compute cosine similarity between observed_embedding and every enrolled person's avg embedding. (4) Filter to candidates with cosine >= TIER2_THRESHOLD (default 0.80). (5) Among those, Tier 1 tag+Jaccard RANKS them. (6) Highest combined rank wins. (7) If NO candidate has cosine >= 0.80, return unmatched.

Tier 1 weights: tag_exact=3.0 (hard gate, not a score), jaccard_identity_markers (range 0-1, multiplied by 1.0). Tier 1 score range: 0.0 (no identity_markers) to 4.0 (tag exact + perfect Jaccard). Tier 1 is used as a tiebreaker among Tier-2-acceptable candidates, not as a gate.

CLIP-ViT-B/32 loads ONCE at module import (infra.person_embedder.py keeps model in module-level singleton). Per-alert cost: ~30-100ms embedding + ~5ms cosine vs all enrolled (numpy matrix multiply). Acceptable for current alert rate.

Mirror animal recognition pattern exactly: VM1 (YOLO) detects bbox -> VM2 (Qwen-VL) returns structured description + better_crop -> CLIP embedding (always, Tier 2) -> cosine sim vs enrolled -> Tier 1 tag+Jaccard ranking among matches -> result.
Better crop selection: pipeline Stage 11b reads vm2_result.better_crop, picks crop_a or crop_b. Falls back to crop_a when better_crop is absent. Same as animal.

Embedding storage: numpy .npz file with named keys = person ids, values = stacked 512-dim float32 arrays. Index file = known_people.json with id + label + identity_markers (set) + first_enrolled_iso + sample_image_paths. Tier-1 signature stored in known_people.json for ranking.

Cosine similarity: standard (A @ B) / (norm_A * norm_B). Threshold initial = 0.80 (CLIP is more discriminative than MegaDescriptor for body shapes; 0.80 balances false-positive vs missed-recognition at small enrollment scale).

person_matcher.match_person() returns: matched=True -> {candidate: {id, label, identity_markers}, cosine_score: float, tier1_score: float, runner_ups: [{id, cosine_score, tier1_score}]}; matched=False -> {top_candidates: [{id, label, cosine_score, tier1_score}], threshold: float}.
Test with synthetic embeddings first (numpy random) before plugging CLIP -- keeps unit tests fast + CPU-only.
Single commit per story on main with US-059 in the message.

stories.title: Add person_matcher/match.py: ALWAYS run CLIP-ViT-B/32 cosine + Tier-1 tag+Jaccard ranking among cosine-acceptable candidates
stories.scope: person_matcher/__init__.py exports match_person(). person_matcher/match.py implements Tier-2-primary matcher. Flow: (1) pick_alert_image_path() from Stage 11b returns chosen crop path. (2) observed_embedding = infra.person_embedder.embed_image(chosen_crop) -> np.ndarray (512,) float32. (3) For each enrolled person: cosine_sim = (observed @ avg) / (norm_obs * norm_avg). Threshold filter: keep only candidates with cosine >= TIER2_THRESHOLD (default 0.80, env var PERSON_MATCH_THRESHOLD overridable). (4) Among cosine-acceptable candidates, compute Tier-1 tag+Jaccard score: tag_exact=3.0 (hard match) + jaccard(identity_markers). (5) Sort by Tier-1 score desc; highest wins. Return shape: matched=True -> {candidate: {id, label, identity_markers}, cosine_score: float, tier1_score: float, runner_ups: [{id, cosine_score, tier1_score}]}; matched=False -> {top_candidates: [{id, label, cosine_score, tier1_score}], threshold: 0.80}. Empty enrolled: matched=False immediately. Lazy-load CLIP-ViT-B/32 inside match_person() (not at module import) so unit tests can run without the model. Storage load: opens data/known/people/embeddings.npz + known_people.json. Unit tests pass storage dicts directly.

stories.notes: Combined-rank weighting: cosine_score (range [-1, 1], typically [0.5, 0.95]) and tier1_score (range [0.0, 4.0]) on different scales. Recommended approach: rank_score = tier1_score + 3.0 * cosine_score (cosine on [0,1] scaled to ~[0,3] range so it carries meaningful weight, plus tier1 on [0,4]). Simpler alternative: pure tier-1-rank among cosine-acceptable candidates (no weighted combination, just sort by tier1 desc). Worker decides and documents. Tier 2 (cosine) ALWAYS runs per operator directive -- no early-out based on Tier 1. Storage load: opens data/known/people/embeddings.npz + known_people.json via person_matcher/storage.py.

stories.title: Tune BOTH thresholds (Tier-1 VM2-feature score + Tier-2 CLIP cosine) against held-out person
stories.scope: scripts/tune_person_threshold.py: load N person crops (from staging area or operator-provided), compute Tier-1 score matrix: each crop's identity_markers scored against (a) enrolled person signature + (b) a held-out 'other person' signature (synthetic: different identity_markers, same build/height/skin_tone). Find Tier-1 score distribution that cleanly separates enrolled from other person. Embed all crops via CLIP-ViT-B/32; compute cosine sim vs enrolled avg + vs synthetic 'other person' avg. CRITICAL: Tier-2 cosine is the primary accept gate. Find Tier-2 cosine threshold (initial guess 0.80) that maximizes recall while rejecting the synthetic 'other person'. Output: docs/person-threshold-tuning.md with recommended threshold + reasoning. Update PRD US-059f acceptance criteria + add recommended values to person_matcher/config.py.
